scope: Explain why the recorded old kernel hash differs from the two newly generated kernels; no rebuild, generation, or numerical/model run.

attribution.classification: build-path-dependent binary difference; not evidence of different numerical kernel source or flags
attribution.embedded_source_filename: gfortran embeds the generated absolute path to mie_scatter_realK.f in the Fortran runtime diagnostic string in .rodata.
attribution.path_length_effect: The expanded-run source path is 8 bytes longer than the retained old artifact path. The .rodata string changes accordingly; 26 differing bytes in .text are all RIP-relative displacement bytes increased by 8 to address data shifted by the longer string. Normalized disassembly showed no other instruction differences.
attribution.build_id: GNU build-id differs as expected because the linked ELF bytes differ.
other_observations: All compared libraries are 20,264 bytes and have identical section sizes/layout, GNU Fortran .comment, dynamic dependencies, and .eh_frame/.eh_frame_hdr contents.
The expanded and direct generated libraries each embed their own run-specific absolute source path and therefore have distinct build IDs and hashes.
limits: The original old binary at the original build path is no longer present; attribution used the old recorded SHA and a retained library whose SHA matches it exactly.

This is a static binary-difference diagnosis, not a fresh functional equivalence test. The differing relative operands point to the shifted diagnostic string, but binary hashes are not identical and should not be reported as bitwise reproducible.

pinned_kernel_sources_and_build.adaptation: Four CMPLX constructors explicitly preserve KIND=RealK; no other source changes
